secrets.notes: Generate .env.local from Bitwarden Secrets Manager via env_localctl.py compile. Dev naming is function-oriented and intentionally narrowed to the minimal local startup set plus feature-test additions.
Compile-first Bitwarden flow. Staging naming is provider-oriented and should map to the real upstream credential or infrastructure secret in use.
Compile-first Bitwarden flow with elevated access controls. Production naming should remain provider-oriented and operationally precise.

namingByEnvironmentRole.dev: Function-oriented naming is allowed. Keys may describe the capability under test, such as default/lowcost/pics.
namingByEnvironmentRole.staging: Provider-oriented naming is preferred. Keys should identify the concrete provider or infrastructure secret in use.
namingByEnvironmentRole.prod: Provider-oriented naming is required for operational clarity, failover control, and rotation ownership.

layers.description: Minimum secrets required to boot the application and authenticate safely.
Secrets only required when a specific capability is enabled, such as verification delivery, image generation, object storage, or Redis-backed runtime features.
Credentials used to control LLM routing and failover. Dev may use capability-oriented logical refs, while staging and prod should still map those refs to concrete provider credentials.
